The actions described in the paragraph appear to be compliant with legal standards. The text explicitly states that the employees were already working the maximum hours permitted by local labor laws. By extending working hours without increasing pay, the employer is not violating regulations regarding overtime pay or maximum working hours, as the employees are not exceeding the legal limit. The management's claim of a "one-time exception" does not inherently violate labor laws if the total hours remain within the statutory maximum and no other labor rights (such as mandatory rest periods or minimum wage requirements) are breached. Therefore, based solely on the information provided, there is no indication of non-compliance with local labor laws.
